title: Product copy, text density, naming and consent

questions.text: What can the UI show instead of saying it (state, preview, default, example, disabled reason)? What is the word budget, and which one sentence must survive?
For every claim about product behaviour in this copy: what is its source (code path, spec line, owner quote)? No source, no claim.
Have I rendered this with >= 5 real records and the extreme values (longest, shortest, empty)?
Does every heading carry instance-specific information? Does every proactive item have one specific fact and one one-tap action?
Is every term the user's word? Is any internal or ops term left?
Which established pattern governs this surface (consent, form, error, empty state), and does the copy follow it?
What default name or value does a newly created item get? Create ten in a row: are they distinct and meaningful? Which field is asked first?
For a changelog, announcement or release note: does each item name something the user can now see or do? Internal changes stay out.
Is every new name in the glossary, and unique to one concept?
Which house rules apply here, and does each one have a lint (houseRules in .jstack/unslop.json) that will catch me?

budgets.measure: word count of rendered card text
word count of rendered modal text

rules.title: Hedge or filler word in user-facing text (simply, seamlessly, easily...)
rules.why: Filler costs reading time and promises ease the UI has to deliver anyway.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the word is in a user-facing string
rules.fixHint: delete it; if the sentence collapses, the UI should show it instead

rules.title: Meta-narration ('This screen lets you...', 'Below you will find...')
rules.pattern: \b(?:this (?:screen|page|section|panel|modal) (?:lets|allows|helps) you|below you(?:'ll| will) find|here you can|in this (?:screen|page|section),? you)\b
rules.why: Explains the UI instead of making it obvious; nobody reads it.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the phrase is in a user-facing string
rules.fixHint: remove; use a specific heading or an example instead

rules.title: Generic heading value (Overview, Insights, Summary, Details...)
rules.why: A heading that says nothing gives no information scent.
rules.confirm: render: heading-only read-through of 5 real records shows identical headings
rules.fixHint: name the instance: a subject, number or date

rules.title: 'You agree' / terms text with no link next to it
rules.why: Assent without a linked, conspicuous notice is weak (Meyer v. Uber, 2017).
rules.confirm: render: DOM test finds no a[href] to the terms in the notice

rules.title: Cards whose text differs only in one slot
rules.why: Template text dominates the data; users stop reading.
rules.confirm: measurement: pairwise token Jaccard > 0.8 across rendered cards for different entities

rules.title: Copy claims product behaviour with no source
rules.why: The agent filled a gap with plausible framing; it may contradict the spec.
rules.confirm: repro-script: claim-to-source table with an empty source cell

rules.title: New items get one constant default name or label
rules.why: Every created thing looks the same, so lists become unreadable and people rename by hand.
rules.confirm: render: create 3 items with no input; their names are identical

rules.title: Release note or announcement item that describes an internal change the user never sees
rules.why: Readers learn the note is noise and stop reading the items that matter.
rules.confirm: repro-script: table item -> screen and element where the user sees it; an empty cell

verify.text: prose lint (house banned words, jargon, hedges) over every locale file
word counts per component and readability per new string vs the budget
render with real data at 375 px and desktop; contact sheet; axe link names and contrast
pairwise similarity across rendered cards; heading-only read-through
claim-to-source table for copy that describes behaviour
